hints: Look closely at the name PVC and remember what atoms must be in its polymer chain besides carbon and hydrogen.
PVC is poly(chloroethene), so its repeat unit is $\text{-CH}_2\text{-CHCl-}$ and complete combustion must also release that chlorine as $\text{HCl}$.
Think about which combustion product is always a greenhouse gas, and what $\text{HCl}$ does when it dissolves in water used to scrub exhaust gases.
walkthrough:
**Recall what PVC is made from**

Think of PVC as polyvinyl chloride, also called poly(chloroethene). Its chain contains C, H and Cl.

Repeat unit:
$$\text{-CH}_2\text{-CHCl-}_n$$

**Write what complete combustion must give**

Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon gives $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Because chlorine is present here, $\text{HCl}$ must form as well.

Overall idea:
$$\text{PVC + O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{HCl}$$

**Check the statements**

$\text{CO}_2$ is a well known greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming, so that statement is true. $\text{HCl}$ is acidic and hazardous, so the products are not just $\text{CO}_2$ and water, scrubber water becomes acidic not alkaline, and exhaust gases must be treated.

options.A: Correct. Complete combustion of PVC produces $\text{CO}_2$ along with $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{HCl}$. $\text{CO}_2$ is a greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming.
options.B: False. This is the trap of treating PVC like a normal hydrocarbon. Because PVC contains chlorine, $\text{HCl}$ is an extra product in addition to $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
options.C: False. $\text{HCl}$ gas dissolves in scrubber water to form hydrochloric acid. The water becomes acidic, with pH below 7, not alkaline.
options.D: False. $\text{HCl}$ is a corrosive, acidic and hazardous gas. Exhaust gases from burning PVC must be scrubbed or treated before release.
